identity.title: Relationship between CH3OD Abundance and Temperature in the Orion KL Nebula

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present high-angular resolution observations of Orion KL using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array to map small-scale changes in column density across the nebula, which provide a new avenue to examine the deuterium chemistry during star and planet formation.
Observations of Orion KL were taken in ALMA Band 4 during Cycle 5 (project code: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.01149, PI: Wilkins) on 2017 December 14, completely on the main 12-m array.

question.value: What is the relationship between gas-phase CH3OD column density and local line-of-sight temperature across Orion KL at sub-arcsecond resolution, and what does it reveal about grain-surface versus gas-phase D-H exchange chemistry?

evidence.quote: By considering how column densities vary with temperature, we find evidence of chemical processes that can significantly alter the observed column densities.

This allows us to plot gas-phase as a function of the local line-of-site temperature across relatively small scales within the nebula and explore temperature-dependent chemical processes that may affect the observed chemistry.
Observations of Orion KL were taken in ALMA Band 4 during Cycle 5 (project code: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.01149, PI: Wilkins) on 2017 December 14, completely on the main 12-m array.
Projected baselines were between 15.1 m and 3.3 km (7.6 and 1650 k$\lambda$, where $\lambda\sim2$ mm is the wavelength), and the primary beam was 39.1$^{\prime\prime}$.

claims.experiment: Map CH3OD column density across Orion KL at ~0.7" resolution using ALMA Band 4 observations, plot column density as a function of rotational temperature, and compare the excess column density profile against an analytical model of grain-surface D-H exchange (based on Souda 2003 and Faure 2015) and thermal desorption.
claims.result: The CH3OD column density vs. temperature profile exhibits a steep rise starting at ~110 K (the 'shark-tooth' feature) up to ~125 K, which is well-matched by a thermal desorption and D-H exchange model with a heating timescale of t_h = 10^3 yr.
claims.finding: Observational data support rapid grain-surface D-H exchange at methanol's hydroxyl site between ~100 and 125 K followed by desorption.

claims.hypothesis: The sharp drop in enhanced CH3OD column density above ~180 K is caused by gas-phase chemical destruction (either protonation followed by dissociative recombination, or neutral-radical reaction with OH).
claims.experiment: Evaluate dissociative recombination branching ratios from KIDA, inspect the 13CH3OH column density profile above 180 K, calculate reaction rates with OH at ~200 K, and map the spatial distribution of power-law-subtracted CH3OD column density and [CH3OD]/[13CH3OH].
claims.result: Dissociative recombination destroys methanol (only 3% branching ratio reproduces methanol) while no drop in 13CH3OH is observed above 180 K; reaction with OH is too slow at ~200 K; excess CH3OD is spatially localized to the Hot Core-SW where gas temperatures max out around 180-200 K.
claims.finding: Gas-phase chemical destruction is refuted as the cause of the drop above 180 K; instead, the drop is due to environment because enhanced deuteration is localized to the Hot Core-SW where little gas exists above 180 K.

why_this_data.value: Orion KL is the nearest high-mass star-forming region (~388 pc), allowing sub-arcsecond (~0.7", ~270 au) ALMA observations to resolve small-scale sub-environments; observing all lines in a single LO setup ensures relative flux uncertainties are dominated by thermal noise rather than calibration uncertainty.

evidence.quote: At a distance of $\sim$388 pc,(cite: Kounkel2017) Orion KL is uniquely situated to explore the relationship between relative deuterated methanol abundances and environmental conditions because sub-environments within the nebula can be resolved, even with modest imaging capabilities.

All spectra were obtained in a single local oscillator set-up consisting of 10 spectral windows; as such, the uncertainties for quantities derived from these spectra are dominated by thermal noise and mostly unaffected by calibration uncertainty.

why_this_method.value: Splitting measurement sets to baselines <=500 m matches the imaging of Wilkins (2022) and recovers flux representative of single-dish observations while resolving small-scale variations; assuming the rotational temperature profile of 13CH3OH is valid because the transitions of both isotopologues have similar upper state energies E_u.

evidence.quote: The data introduced here were prepared in the same way as the images presented by (cite: Wilkins2022) In brief, the data cubes were created from measurement sets split to include only baselines of $\le$500 m, resulting in a synthesized beam of $0.\!\!^{\prime\prime}74\times0.\!\!^{\prime\prime}63$.

The rotational temperature ($T_{\rm rot}$) profile was assumed to be the same as that previously derived(cite: Wilkins2022) from since the transitions of both isotopologues have similar upper energy states $E_u$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Longer heating timescales (t_h >= 10^4 yr) in the thermal desorption model were rejected because they do not follow the increasing column density profile as closely as t_h = 10^3 yr.

evidence.quote: The resulting desorption model from eq [\[eqn:desrate\]](#eqn:desrate) with $t_h=10^3$ yr is shown by the black dashed line in Figure [\[fig:nvt\]](#fig:nvt)a. Longer timescales (i.e., $t_h\ge10^4$ yr) characteristic of massive YSOs do not follow the increasing profile as closely.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gas-phase D-H exchange via protonation of the hydroxyl group followed by dissociative recombination was rejected as an explanation for the CH3OD drop above 180 K because dissociative recombination destroys methanol (only 3% branching ratio forms methanol) and no corresponding drop is seen in 13CH3OH.

referee_caveats_inferred: The CH3OD column density derivation does not fit rotational temperature independently; it fixes T_rot to the map previously derived from 13CH3OH in Wilkins et al. (2022), assuming co-spatial emission and identical excitation temperatures.

There is a minor numerical inconsistency in the text regarding the initial gas-phase CH3OD column density assumed in the toy desorption model (stated as 1e16 cm^-2 in one paragraph and 9.0e15 cm^-2 in the next).
Only three CH3OD lines are fitted per pixel, making the column density sensitive to line blending in the crowded spectrum of Orion KL.
